Family Discovery Interview: The opening conversation that establishes who this family is before anything is recommended.
A written intake the advisor works from for years.
Family Intelligence Profile: A single view of a family's strengths, risks, and unasked questions.
One page the advisor reads before every meeting.
Family Relationship Map: A diagram of who actually talks to whom across the generations.
A visible map of where the relationships are thin.
Family Story Interview: The first structured capture of how this family came to be.
A transcript that becomes source material for everything after.
Wealth Origin Story: The account of where the money came from and what it cost.
A narrative the next generation can repeat accurately.
Family Priority Finder: A sorting exercise for families with more concerns than capacity.
A ranked list of what gets attention this year.
Family Transition Timeline: A view of the changes coming in the next decade.
A dated timeline of what must be ready and when.
Family Influence Map: Identifies who the family actually listens to, inside and outside the house.
A named list of the voices that carry weight.
Family Concern Inventory: A private capture of what each member is quietly worried about.
A themed summary of concerns nobody had said aloud.
Family Opportunity Map: Names what is possible for this family that they have not considered.
A short list of openings worth pursuing.
Family Values Assessment: A scored read on the values operating in the house versus the values claimed.
A gap report between stated and lived values.
Values Card Sort: A tactile exercise that forces a family from forty values to five.
Five values chosen out loud, together.
Values Definition Guide: Turns a one-word value into a sentence the family agrees on.
A written definition for each chosen value.
Values-to-Behavior Map: Converts each value into an observable practice.
A behavior list a grandchild could recognize.
Family Identity Exercise: Names what makes this family recognizably itself.
A paragraph the family would sign.
Shared Beliefs Conversation: A guided conversation about what this family holds true.
A record of agreements and honest differences.
Family Culture Assessment: Measures the unwritten rules of the household.
A description of the culture as it currently operates.
Traditions Inventory: Catalogs what this family repeats and why.
A list of traditions worth keeping and worth retiring.
Family Strengths Profile: Names the family's real capacities rather than its aspirations.
A strengths summary used to assign responsibility.
Family Identity Statement: The family's own description of itself in one page.
A signed statement the family displays.
Personal Purpose Assessment: A structured read on what one person is actually built for.
A purpose statement with evidence behind it.
Family Purpose Builder: Moves a family from individual purpose to shared purpose.
A single sentence naming what this family is for.
Retirement Purpose Guide: For the person whose identity has been their work.
A plan for the first year after the title goes away.
Founder Next-Chapter Plan: Names what a founder does with the decades after the exit.
A written next chapter with commitments attached.
Purpose and Wealth Alignment: Tests whether the money is serving the stated purpose.
A list of where resources and purpose have drifted apart.
Contribution Discovery Exercise: Finds the specific contribution only this person can make.
A named contribution with a first step.
Calling Conversation: A guided conversation about vocation and calling across generations.
A record of what each person believes they are called to.
Personal Mission Statement: One person's own statement of intent.
Family Mission Statement: The household's shared statement of intent.
A framed statement the family agreed to together.
Purpose-Based Decision Guide: A filter for decisions that money alone cannot settle.
A written decision filter the family applies.
Family Communication Assessment: Measures how this family actually talks about hard things.
A scored read with the specific breakdown points named.
Family Listening Exercise: Trains the family to hear before responding.
A practiced habit and a record of what was heard.
Relationship Coverage Map: Shows which relationships in the family nobody is tending.
A coverage map with the gaps circled.
Sibling Relationship Guide: For adult siblings who will one day decide together.
An honest conversation held before it is required.
Family Trust Assessment: Measures the trust that any transfer depends on.
A trust reading by relationship pair.
Difficult Conversation Planner: Prepares a specific hard conversation before it happens.
A drafted opening and the likely responses.
Reconciliation Conversation Guide: For a relationship that has been distant or broken.
A first conversation with a realistic goal.
Family Care Plan: Names who cares for whom as the generations age.
A written care plan with names attached.
Relationship Strengthening Journey: A sustained practice rather than a single conversation.
A month of small, repeated relational actions.
Annual Family Relationship Review: A yearly honest read on how the family is doing.
A dated review the family repeats each year.
Marriage and Money Assessment: Surfaces where a couple actually disagrees about money.
A side-by-side comparison of two private answers.
Shared Financial Vision: Moves a couple from two financial pictures to one.
A written vision both spouses signed.
Couple Values Conversation: The values conversation done first as two, then as a family.
An agreed values list before the children weigh in.
Retirement Expectations Guide: Surfaces the assumptions each spouse holds and has never said.
Spousal Financial Confidence Assessment: Measures whether both spouses could actually carry the finances alone.
A readiness score and the specific gaps.
Blended-Family Conversation: For families where the tree has more than one trunk.
A conversation about fairness, held before the will is read.
Couple Generosity Plan: A giving plan the couple builds together.
Surviving-Spouse Preparedness: Prepares the spouse who will most likely be left.
A binder, a contact list, and a rehearsed first ninety days.
Couple Legacy Statement: The couple's shared statement of what they hope to leave.
A joint statement written before the family sees it.
Annual Couple Financial Review: A yearly rhythm rather than a crisis conversation.
A dated review the couple keeps.
Parenting Wealth Guide: For parents raising children in more resources than they had.
A parenting approach with specific practices.
Grandparent Wisdom Interview: Captures a grandparent's judgment while it is still available.
A recorded interview and a written transcript.
Family Responsibility Ladder: Age-appropriate responsibility, mapped from childhood to adulthood.
A ladder with each child's current rung marked.
Age-Based Money Conversations: What to say about money at six, at sixteen, at twenty-six.
Children and Generosity Guide: Teaches giving as joy rather than as duty.
A child-led giving practice the family repeats.
Family Work-Ethic Plan: Deliberate transmission of the work ethic that built the wealth.
A written plan with real assignments.
Preparing Children for Wealth: A staged preparation plan by age and readiness.
Grandparent Legacy Letter: A grandparent's written words to a grandchild.
A letter delivered or kept for a named date.
Family Mentoring Plan: Pairs the generations deliberately rather than hoping.
Named mentor pairs with a meeting rhythm.
Intergenerational Learning Calendar: Puts the transmission on a calendar instead of a wish list.
A twelve-month calendar with people attached.
Heir Readiness Assessment: An honest read on whether an heir is prepared for what is coming.
A readiness score with named development needs.
Financial Literacy Journey: Structured financial formation for the rising generation.
A completed literacy pathway with demonstrated competence.
Trustee Readiness Assessment: Evaluates whether a family member should serve as trustee.
A recommendation with reasoning the family can review.
Rising-Generation Ownership Readiness: Assesses readiness to own rather than to operate.
Rising-Generation Purpose Guide: Helps an heir find purpose that is not inherited.
A personal direction statement in their own words.
Family History Learning Guide: Teaches the next generation the story they will carry.
A learned history the young can retell.
Next-Generation Discussion Guide: A conversation with the rising generation rather than about them.
A record of what they actually said.
Responsibility Development Plan: A staged plan for handing over real responsibility.
A dated plan with assignments and review points.
Mentor Matching Guide: Pairs each heir with the right voice, inside or outside the family.
Named pairings with a first meeting scheduled.
Annual Heir Development Plan: A yearly plan for preparing the people, not the assets.
A dated development plan per heir.
Financial Wisdom Assessment: Measures wisdom rather than knowledge about money.
A scored profile with the practices to strengthen.
Family Money Story: Traces the beliefs about money this family inherited.
A written money story with the patterns named.
Spending and Lifestyle Conversation: An honest conversation about how this family actually lives.
An agreed lifestyle standard the family names.
Saving and Investing Foundations: Foundational competence for the rising generation.
Debt and Responsibility Guide: Teaches obligation, leverage, and the cost of both.
A family position on debt, written down.
Financial Independence Plan: For the young adult moving from support to self-sufficiency.
A dated independence plan with milestones.
Wise Decision-Making Tool: A repeatable filter for significant financial decisions.
A written decision framework the family uses.
Contentment Exercise: Addresses the appetite that no amount of money satisfies.
A named practice that interrupts accumulation.
Stewardship Priorities Worksheet: Orders the family's financial priorities against its convictions.
A ranked priority list the family signed.
Annual Financial Wisdom Journey: A yearly formation rhythm rather than a one-time class.
A completed annual journey with reflections kept.
Wealth Transfer Readiness Assessment: Measures whether the people are as ready as the plan.
A readiness gap report across the family.
Beneficiary Understanding Guide: Ensures beneficiaries understand what they are receiving and why.
Estate Communication Planner: Plans what is said, to whom, and in what order.
A written communication sequence with dates.
Inheritance Preparation Journey: Prepares the receiver over months rather than minutes.
Fairness Versus Equality Exercise: Addresses the question that causes most inheritance conflict.
A stated family position on fairness.
Trust Purpose Conversation: Explains the why behind the structure, not just the terms.
A written statement of intent alongside the trust.
Distribution Readiness Guide: Determines whether a distribution should happen yet.
A go or wait recommendation with reasoning.
Wealth Transfer Timeline: Sequences the transfer over years rather than at once.
Family Estate Meeting Kit: The meeting where intentions are said out loud.
A facilitated meeting and a written record.
Post-Inheritance Support Plan: Support in the year after the money arrives.
A twelve-month support plan per heir.
Governance Readiness Assessment: Determines whether a family needs governance yet, and which kind.
A recommendation with the right structure named.
Family Meeting Agenda Builder: Builds an agenda out of the family's own answers.
A printed agenda for the next meeting.
Decision Rights Map: Names who decides what before the disagreement.
A decision rights chart the family agreed to.
Family Council Builder: Establishes the body where the family governs itself.
A constituted council with terms and a calendar.
Family Constitution Builder: The written agreement a family governs by.
Governance Policy Guide: Turns repeated arguments into settled policy.
Written policies covering the recurring questions.
Shared Asset Decision Guide: For the cabin, the land, the thing everyone owns together.
A written agreement on use, cost, and exit.
Family Employment Policy: Settles who can work in the business and on what terms.
A written employment policy adopted in advance.
Conflict Resolution Policy: Names how this family will handle disagreement before it has one.
An agreed process with a named third party.
Annual Governance Review: A yearly check on whether the structures still fit.
A dated review with amendments recorded.
